Gillard government. They said, as per paragraph C7, before public release of the homogenised
dataset, the Bureau should determine and document the reasons why the new dataset shows a lower
average temperature in the period prior to 1940 than is shown by data from whole network and
previous international analysis. When you just said there before that was the warmest
winter on record, was that quoting actual observations or the homogenised data from
either ACORN 1 or ACORN 2? I'd say it'd be both. I'm just going on the
observed record during this winter. It's the warmest winter on record since...
So what have you got to say about this that says, the independent peer review that says
you homogenised data records down prior to 1940? So I'm not sure what your question is,
Senator. Well my question is, have you answered the question of the independent peer review
that wanted to know why you homogenised records, i.e. you took take the original
recordings and then you've changed them and you've pushed them down to make it look like
temperature records have increased? Dr Stone will address this.
Sure, that's a correct interpretation of the review. That's exactly what the correct
interpretation is. The Bureau has completed 30 of the 31 recommendations in that review,
just directly addressing the point you've made about homogenisation.
If the observation network never changed, it would show a warming trend
greater than that that we currently estimate. That's not true, that actually is not...
No, I'm sorry, that is true because of the chart.
So why ask? Because you've got a range of documents there that the rest of us do not.
I wonder if you would care to... Table.
To table those. Absolutely.
And place the questions related to the finite information that you've obviously got flagged
and highlighted there on notice so that we can get accurate response.
Because that was a misleading response. That's fine.
